description:
Generate a visual diagram from a structured graph of nodes and edges, and save it to an existing CanvasKeep diagram.

You provide the logical structure (what components exist and how they connect), and CanvasKeep handles all visual layout automatically - do NOT try to compute x/y positions.

NODES: Create one node for every distinct component, actor, system, service, or data store mentioned in the user's request. Give each a short, clear label (under 30 chars). Choose the right type for visual distinction.

EDGES: Create one edge for every meaningful interaction, data flow, API call, or dependency between nodes. Label edges with the nature of the interaction (e.g. 'REST API', 'SQL query', 'WebSocket', 'publishes'). Every important relationship should be an edge.

MODE: Use 'replace' (default) to create a fresh diagram. Use 'append' to add new elements alongside existing content in the diagram.

diagram_id.description: The diagram UUID to write the generated content into. Create one first with create_diagram if needed.

direction.description: Layout direction. 'vertical' (default): top-to-bottom flow, best for sequential processes. 'horizontal': left-to-right. 'auto': picks based on max fan-out from any single node.

edges.description: Connections between nodes representing interactions, data flows, API calls, or dependencies. Each becomes a labeled arrow.

from.description: The id of the source node where this connection starts

label.description: A short label shown on the arrow describing the interaction (e.g. 'HTTP request', 'SQL query', 'publishes events'). Omit if the relationship is obvious from context.

to.description: The id of the target node where this connection ends

mode.description: 'replace' clears existing content and draws only the new graph. 'append' adds the new graph alongside any existing diagram content.

nodes.description: Every distinct component, actor, system, or data store to show on the diagram. Each becomes a labeled box.

id.description: A unique identifier for this node, used to reference it in edges (e.g. 'api-gateway', 'user-db')

label.description: A short human-readable label shown inside the box on the diagram (e.g. 'API Gateway', 'User Database'). Keep it under 30 characters for best readability.

type.description: Visual style hint. 'process' (purple, default): internal logic or computation. 'service' (green): a running service or microservice. 'datastore' (blue): a database, cache, or storage system. 'external' (yellow, dashed border): an external system or third-party API outside your control.

name: generate_diagram
